resources.string: Your onn remote. Your TV volume.
Volume and mute are sent to your TV over your local network. Android volume stays fixed.
TV and onn button reader connected
Only the Samsung path has been tested on a real TV. Other adapters are experimental; use the test buttons first.
Cannot reach the Samsung TV. Check its address and local-network access.
Saved. Approve onn Volume on the TV if prompted.
Enable the relay before testing a volume button.
Check the TV address, protocol, port and credentials.
Relays volume and mute to your selected TV. Reads only volume events from the authorized onn remote over local ADB. Cannot read screen contents.
Remove saved TV credentials and pause the relay?
Turn on your TV and connect it to the same Wi-Fi or home network as your onn. We’ll look for your TV and identify its system when possible.
What kind of TV do you have?
Samsung with TizenOS: connect below, then choose Allow on the TV when it asks about onn Volume.
Roku TV: enable Control by mobile apps in its advanced system settings. Choose this for TCL or Hisense only if the TV runs Roku OS. Experimental.
Sony BRAVIA: enable IP control on the TV. Enter its pre-shared key below if you set one. This is for compatible BRAVIA TVs, not every Google TV. Experimental.
Advanced option: enter a writable RenderingControl endpoint and its port/path. Not every TV supports it. Experimental.
TV not found? Set up manually
Possible TV — check the TV system
No TV advertised itself. This does not mean it is incompatible. Enter the TV address manually, and check that both devices use the same network.
Not found? Look under Network / Connection in the TV settings for its IP address.
Enter the private IP address shown in your TV network settings.
This is your first connection to this address. Continue only if it is your TV. The app will remember this certificate and refuse a different one later.
TV connected. Continue to set up your remote.
Waiting for the TV. Check that it is on and approve onn Volume if asked.
A few one-time settings let this app receive your volume buttons. You choose each permission in Android.

1. Open Developer options and turn on USB debugging. If Developer options are hidden, open Settings → Device preferences / System → About and select Android TV OS build 7 times. Keep debugging on while using the bridge, on a trusted network.
2. In Accessibility, choose onn Volume Bridge and enable it. The app receives remote buttons; it cannot read your screen.
3. Return here. In the USB debugging prompt, check Always allow and choose Allow. This connects the app to this onn box only. No PC is needed afterward.
Remote not connected yet. Check debugging and its permission prompt.
4. Open remote settings. Set Volume control to Automatic (CEC). Keep your existing power-button setup. If normal CEC already controls TV volume, use that instead of enabling this bridge.
First, try these buttons. The volume indicator should appear on your TV.
Now use the real onn remote: press + and −, hold one briefly, then release. Try Mute and the arrows / OK too. Only TV volume should change, and holding should stop when you release.
I tested the onn remote and it works.

App buttons fail: check the TV address, network-control settings and on-TV pairing.

App buttons work, remote does not: go Back and check accessibility, USB debugging and Always allow.

Both TV and onn volume change: check Automatic (CEC). If CEC alone controls TV volume, pause this bridge.

Changes continue after release: pause the bridge and reconnect before testing again.
Use your onn remote as usual. The bridge works on the box without a PC. Keep your TV on the same network. You can pause it here at any time.
One button prepares your remote. The app will enable its own volume helper using a local connection you approve. Android may ask you to turn on USB debugging and choose Always allow.
Setting up… approve USB debugging if asked
One Android setting needs your approval

Turn on USB debugging in Developer options, then return here. Setup will continue automatically. If Developer options are hidden: Settings → System / Device preferences → About → select Android TV OS build 7 times. Keep debugging on while using this app on a trusted network.
Your box does not yet report fixed HDMI volume. In remote settings, choose Volume control → Automatic (CEC), then return here. The app will check it again. Keep your existing power-button setup.

Check that USB debugging is on and approve the prompt with Always allow. Then retry. If your firmware does not expose local debugging or refuses the setting, use manual setup; the app cannot grant itself this access.
